To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phospholipase activating protein (PLP) is a novel regulator of leukotrienes and thromboxane production.

leukotriene-D4 stimulates the release of arachidate from endothelial and smooth muscle cells by activating phospholipase-A2, that this activation is mediated by a protein that is present in the cytoplasmic fraction of these cells and that this protein, which we have called phospholipase-activating protein (PLAP), has been partially purified and characterized.
leukotrienes can induce the production of thromboxane B, by smooth muscle cells, which is required for the contractile effect of leukotrienes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of leukotrienes in smooth muscle and the possible roles of cyclooxygenases in mediating these effects.
the mechanism by which leukotrienes cause smooth muscle contraction, in particular, with the possible role of thromboxane synthesis.
the mechanism of action of the leukotriennes in the lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of cyclooxygenases and thromboxane synthesis in leukotriene-mediated contraction is tissue-dependent and that the source of the thromboxanes is not known.
leukotriene-mediated responses are dependent on the cyclooxygenases and that the cyclooxygenasedependent component may be due to thromboxane B production by either platelets or smooth muscle.

the role of cyclooxygenases in leukotriene action remains to be established in most tissues, although in some tissues, particularly the vasculature and lung parenchymal tissue, cyclooxygenase may be important.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phospholipase C is the primary mediator of leukotrienes in smooth muscle, but that phospholipases A2 are involved as well.

the role of thromboxane in mediating leukotrriene responses is not yet known and that thromboxane synthesis by a number of cell types, including smooth muscle and endothelium, may be important in this process (4).
we are studying the mechanism of action of a group of compounds called leukotrienes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leukotriens, particularly LTC4 and LTD4, are potent spasmogen in a variety of different tissues, including the lung, ileum, and vasculature.
the PLAP gene is a novel gene in this pathway.
phospholipase activating protein (PLAA) plays a role in regulating thromboxane synthesis in response to leukotrienes.
